raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
human notes:
1. this is a skill used to draft a new model support in torchtitan so one can iterate with agents with the draft, 
2. covering model definition, parallelisms, numerical parity, feature and e2e tests,
3. following 1) titan coding styles in naming, comments, file structure, 2) proper reusing existing modules, abstract boundaries. 

## Why

The add_model guidance predates current TorchTitan APIs and needs a concrete validation plan for new model ports. A numerical golden is useful only after the debug recipe is proven repeatable.

## Changes

- Document current flavor/build, recipe, lifecycle, sharding, checkpoint, and shared component APIs.
- Require component and full-model forward parity in evaluation and training, plus gradients for differentiable components and the full training model. Select compatible HF, Megatron, author, SGLang, or vLLM references.
- Keep CPU feature tests, real combined FSDP/TP/EP/PP training, and strict debug goldens. Prove independent repeatability with full-precision loss and grad_norm before golden export and replay.
- Add offline parallelism comparisons with matched global batches and loss normalization, reconstructed gradients before clipping, and global norm scaling checks. Report the matrix evidence in the PR.
- Require PR stacks: model enablement, additional parallelisms and required kernels, then optional performance work. Reuse established attention/remat paths and benchmark matched workloads when requested.
- Require local `pr_review` -> revise -> re-review for every PR until the current version is approved with no open must-fix findings. Re-review affected dependencies before submission; use concise API examples and a compact coverage table.

## Example

A new MoE port first adds its model, FSDP, and reference forward/backward tests.
A later PR adds TP/EP/PP support and the broader numerical comparisons.
A TP run reporting grad_norm 2.0 against a matched baseline of 1.0 requires investigation.
The matrix checks gradients before clipping, so clipping cannot conceal the scaling problem.
Each PR is revised and locally reviewed until it passes; then the reviewed stack is submitted.
A fixed debug recipe still needs exactly matching loss and grad_norm before golden generation.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed in an isolated checkout with matching dependencies.
- Checked skill metadata, 15 local links, and eight unchanged Bash/Python example blocks.
- Repeatability command checks previously verified rejection of a one-ULP grad_norm difference; those examples are unchanged.

- Local self-review using `pr-review` passed for `5805da324` against `upstream/main` (`828961319`), with no open must-fix findings. Clarified that new kernels require a demonstrated need and norm ratios compare per-parameter gradients.

This changes documentation only; no GPU training was run.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,288 @@
+---
+name: add_model
+description: Add or port a model to TorchTitan using shared components, model flavors, Python recipes, forward/backward parity, CPU feature tests, parallelism validation, numerical goldens, and locally reviewed PR stacks. Use when the user requests a new model or invokes /add_model.
+---
+
+# Adding a Model to TorchTitan
+
+Build the model in a PR stack. Establish reference correctness and FSDP first,
+then add more parallelisms, any required new kernels, and requested performance work. Batch
+related edits before expensive GPU checks; rerun affected checks after fixes or
+changes to computation. Review every PR locally before submitting the stack.
+
+Follow applicable `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/rules/`
+instructions. Read the current [model guide](../../../torchtitan/models/README.md)
+and [config guide](../../../torchtitan/config/README.md) before choosing an API.
+Repository paths below are relative to the repository root. Verify helpers and
+example harnesses in the checkout before using them.
+
+- Read [numerical_parity.md](references/numerical_parity.md) when building or
+  running reference comparisons.
+- Read [test_coverage.md](references/test_coverage.md) when planning feature
+  tests, combined parallelism training, and remote numerical golden baselines.
+- Read [code_style_checklist.md](references/code_style_checklist.md) for cleanup
+  and the required `pr_review` -> revise -> `pr_review` loop for each PR.
+- When available, use `/numerics_debugging` to localize unexplained drift and
+  `/pyrefly_ci_check` when local type checking disagrees with CI. Model-specific
+  numerical skills can supply an existing harness for that family.
+
+## Phase 0: Scope and reference
+
+1. Identify the model variant, supported tasks, checkpoint and reference-code
+   revisions, and requested parallelisms. Reference candidates include Hugging Face
+   `transformers`, Megatron-LM/Megatron Core, the model author's implementation,
+   SGLang, and vLLM. Choose references that support the exact variant, features,
+   and inference or training checks; pin their revisions.
+2. Inventory attention and sequence boundaries, positional encoding, norms,
+   dense FFN or MoE routing, shared experts, auxiliary objectives, weight tying,
+   and any vision encoder or projector. Compare each with existing components.
+3. Establish the available checkpoints, dependencies, and hardware. Prefer the
+   model's official open weights on Hugging Face Hub when available; record the
+   repository ID and pin the checkpoint revision. Plan three test artifacts:
+   CPU coverage of important/new features, a real-GPU training test combining
+   supported parallelisms, and a debug-recipe numerical golden baseline generated
+   on remote GPUs. Normally reserve 8 H100s for combined FSDP/TP/EP/PP coverage.
+   Also plan forward/backward reference parity, an offline parallelism matrix,
+   convergence, and requested scale validation. Record checks that cannot run.
+4. Plan a stack with this order:
+   - Model definition, FSDP, forward/backward parity, and feature tests.
+   - Additional parallelisms and any required new kernels, with validation.
+   - Performance optimization when requested.
+   Split larger stages further, for example decoder and image encoder support.
+   Each PR must be a working increment with a clear scope and validation plan.
+   Reuse existing attention backends, including FlexAttention and varlen paths,
+   and standard remat integration during initial enablement.
+
+## Phase 1: Model definition and public config API
+
+Reuse the closest model and the shared components before adding code:
+
+| Need | Current location |
+| --- | --- |
+| Model lifecycle, module and adapter contracts | `torchtitan/models/base/` |
+| Decoder blocks and stack | `torchtitan/models/common/decoder.py` |
+| Attention, metadata and CP backends | `torchtitan/models/common/attention/` |
+| RoPE | `torchtitan/models/common/rope.py` (`ComplexRoPE`, `CosSinRoPE`) |
+| Norms and standard module wrappers | `torchtitan/models/common/nn_modules.py`, `torchtitan/models/common/norm.py` |
+| Dense FFN and MoE | `torchtitan/models/common/feed_forward.py`, `torchtitan/models/common/moe/`, `torchtitan/models/common/dist_moe/` |
+| Embedding and linear projections | `torchtitan/models/common/embedding.py`, `torchtitan/models/common/linear/` |
+| Vision and multimodal composition | `torchtitan/models/common/vision_encoder.py`, `torchtitan/models/common/multimodal.py` |
+
+Use `torchtitan/models/common/config_utils.py` factories such as `make_gqa_config`,
+`make_ffn_config`, `make_moe_config`, and `make_router_config` when they express the
+architecture. Keep new concrete shared components in `torchtitan/models/common/`,
+lifecycle contracts in `torchtitan/models/base/`, distributed helpers in
+`torchtitan/distributed/`, and model-specific computation in its model package.
+
+The model package exposes the following API:
+
+- `flavors.py`: `MODEL_FLAVORS` and
+  `build_model_config(flavor, *, parallelism=...)`, returning the concrete
+  model's nested `Config`. Follow sibling builders for supported context lengths,
+  attention backends, and flavor names; include a reduced `debugmodel` fixture.
+- `model.py`: the model and its nested config. Inherit `Decoder` or another
+  matching shared architecture where possible. Models used by the standard
+  engine need `preprocess_inputs`, `Config.get_nparams_and_flops`, and the
+  `BaseModel` lifecycle. Reuse inherited implementations when applicable.
+- `sharding.py`: model-specific sharding constructors, only when shared
+  constructors do not cover the components. Attach sharding to component configs
+  where the flavor builder creates them.
+- `state_dict_adapter.py`: HF/native key and layout mapping. Reuse shared adapter
+  helpers and bind the adapter with the model class's `state_dict_adapter_cls`.
+- `__init__.py`: re-export the model class, `MODEL_FLAVORS`, and
+  `build_model_config` for recipe and checkpoint-conversion consumers.
+
+Keep parameter initialization in configs or `init_states` overrides needed for
+ordering, such as tying weights. Follow the nearest transformer block's remat
+annotations when adding computation; see
+[REMAT.md](../../../torchtitan/distributed/REMAT.md).
+
+Wire stateful training features through `_register_optimizer_hooks` when needed:
+balancing updates, accumulated auxiliary losses, and resets must run at the
+intended optimizer/microbatch boundaries. Follow Kimi K3's quantile-balancing
+hook and Qwen3.5/DeepSeek V4's balancing and auxiliary-loss hooks. Verify training,
+evaluation, and recomputation behavior through the actual trainer path.
+
+Training recipes belong in `torchtitan_recipes/`. Reusable CPU/CI model fixtures
+belong in `torchtitan_recipes/tests/models/`; composed integration configurations
+live with their definitions in `tests/integration_tests/`. Public training
+recipes should describe configurations actually validated for training.
+
+## Phase 2: Establish numerical parity
+
+Use [numerical_parity.md](references/numerical_parity.md):
+
+1. Build the matching model config with `ParallelismConfig()` for the baseline.
+   Match the reference's weights, inputs, masks, positions, dtype, and mode.
+   Reuse the generic checkpoint converter when a native DCP is needed.
+2. Compare each component, one block, any vision/projector path, and full-model
+   outputs in evaluation and training modes. Reuse shared component tests where
+   they cover unchanged math, and verify the port's integration. Record enough
+   reference details to reproduce each comparison.
+3. Check actual tensors with justified absolute and relative tolerances. Report
+   logit/probability metrics as additional evidence. For MoE, validate the router
+   separately and use imposed routing to diagnose the remaining computation.
+4. Compare input gradients where defined and parameter gradients for differentiable
+   components and the full training model. Check normalized training loss,
+   auxiliary objectives, and state updates. Use references that support backward
+   or independent differentiable oracles; record any missing checks as gaps.
+   Revalidate loading when native checkpoint keys, shapes, or layouts change.
+
+## Phase 3: Recipes and distributed execution
+
+1. Construct `ParallelismConfig` first and pass it to `build_model_config`.
+   Sequence and expert parallelism affect the built sharding. Rebuild the model
+   config when those settings change; copying a config or changing degrees later
+   does not reconstruct its layouts.
+2. Reuse `BaseModel.parallelize`: it binds `local_compile_regions`, applies
+   declarative SPMD parallelism, applies `activation_remat`, then applies FSDP.
+   `Decoder` supplies its FSDP implementation. Override lifecycle methods only
+   for a demonstrated model-specific requirement.
+3. Apply optional config transforms in the recipe for CP, async TP, or other
+   supported implementations. Follow
+   [transform/README.md](../../../torchtitan/config/transform/README.md) for ordering
+   and compatibility. Enable registered local compile regions through the model
+   config; FlexAttention manages its own compilation.
+4. Use the shared sharding constructors and canonical mesh-axis order. Match
+   sharding input keys to forward parameter names after shape-suffix renames.
+   Validate mesh axes and placements and document gradient placements for
+   `to_local`, `local_map`, or `full_tensor` boundaries.
+5. Treat preprocessing outputs as explicit contracts: mask and RoPE positions,
+   packed-document boundaries, padding, labels/loss denominators, and modality
+   metadata must survive TP/SP, EP, CP, PP, and data-parallel execution. Test
+   packed inputs against isolated documents and mixed modality presence across
+   ranks where supported.
+6. Reuse the model's pipeline hooks for PP. Extra cross-layer state needs an
+   explicit stage payload, gradient route, and cleanup contract. Choose stage
+   splits that exercise its lifetime and reuse; Kimi K3's attention-residual
+   cache and exact block-gradient tests illustrate this requirement.
+7. Run an offline numerical matrix covering each claimed parallelism and important
+   combinations. Match logical inputs, checkpoints, global batch, and loss
+   normalization. Compare outputs, loss, gradients, and global gradient norms
+   with justified tolerances. Follow
+   [numerical_parity.md](references/numerical_parity.md) for reconstruction and
+   scaling checks. Summarize results in the PR; keep matrix scripts and logs in
+   generated outputs.
+
+Select a recipe with `--module` (its importable module) and `--config` (its factory
+name). Set model, training, parallelism, debug, and remat fields in Python. For
+example, inspect a shipped recipe's model and settings before a launch:
+
+```bash
+python3 - <<'PY'
+from torchtitan.config import ConfigLoader
+
+config = ConfigLoader().load([
+    "--module", "torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.llama3",
+    "--config", "llama3_debugmodel",
+])
+print("model:", type(config.model).__qualname__)
+print("parallelism:", config.parallelism)
+print("debug:", config.debug)
+PY
+```
+
+For a training launch, `NGPU` must match the recipe's physical world size. The
+supported operational CLI options are documented in `torchtitan/config/README.md`.
+
+## Phase 4: Test coverage, cleanup, and lint
+
+Implement all three layers in [test_coverage.md](references/test_coverage.md):
+
+1. **Important feature tests, mostly CPU.** Cover each new computation or
+   stateful feature with independent expected results, edge cases, gradients
+   where applicable, and lifecycle behavior. For quantile balancing, test the
+   histogram/quantile math, padding, bias updates, and accumulation/reset timing.
+   Extend shared flavor/config and adapter contracts as well.
+2. **Combined parallelism training, on real GPUs.** Add a single model training
+   test with FSDP, TP, EP, and PP active together for an MoE model, normally on
+   8 H100s. Dense models cover FSDP/TP/PP and record EP as inapplicable. Verify the
+   built model, mesh, pipeline microbatches, optimizer steps, and feature hooks;
+   mark the definition `use_real_pg=True`. Check that CI selects the entry and
+   hardware. Add focused cases for uncovered model-specific paths.
+3. **Numerical regression golden, from remote GPUs.** Select a reduced debug
+   recipe retaining the important architecture and feature paths. First prove
+   repeatability across at least two independent remote launches, each with
+   at least 10 optimizer steps: seed 42, strict deterministic execution, and
+   bitwise-identical full-precision loss and grad_norm at every step. Then export
+   and commit the small, architecture/mode-specific golden and its provenance,
+   register `golden_numerics_path`, and rerun without export. A deterministic
+   setting alone does not prove repeatability. Reuse the combined training test
+   when repeatable; otherwise establish a deterministic numerical fixture and
+   document the combined test's limitation. Keep golden creation gated on the
+   repeatability proof.
+
+- Maintain the compact coverage table for every component and the full model,
+  including mode, forward/backward checks, reference, recipe/parallelism, and
+  evidence. Commit focused feature tests, the combined integration test, and the
+  golden; report the wider offline matrix in the PR description.
+- For non-computation changes, require bitwise-identical loss and grad_norm with
+  `config.debug.seed = 42` and `config.debug.deterministic = True`, using matching
+  parallelism and GPU settings. Never enable `deterministic_warn_only`. Use
+  `scripts/loss_compare.py` with `--metrics loss,grad_norm --assert-equal` to compare
+  full-precision TensorBoard values. Computation changes require convergence on
+  representative data, such as C4.
+- Run the relevant parity and integration matrix after the implementation and
+  cleanup pass. For performance measurements, use at least 10 training steps.
+- Apply [code_style_checklist.md](references/code_style_checklist.md), then run
+  `pre-commit run --all-files` before review. Resolve local type-check environment
+  differences before allowing a hook to remove unused ignores.
+
+## Phase 5: Performance work when requested
+
+Prepare performance changes as later PRs after correctness and parallelism
+validation. Choose a feasible model, batch, sequence length, and parallelism
+config for the available hardware, then submit benchmark jobs with the cluster's
+supported launcher. Compare matching workloads: training with HF/Megatron and
+supported inference paths with HF/vLLM/SGLang, matching prefill/decode and cache
+settings. Record dtype, backend, kernels, compilation, and hardware. Use at least
+10 measured optimizer steps after warmup for training; report throughput, step
+time, and peak memory. Use `local-compile-perf` when available for compile tuning,
+and revalidate numerics after changes.
+
+## Phase 6: Scale validation when requested
+
+Run multi-node training when it is part of the requested validation and the
+needed resources are available. Use the target cluster's supported launcher,
+compiler, communication stack, and dependency versions; configure persistent
+output storage through `--output-dir`. Investigate failures in both the model's
+distributed behavior and its launch environment. Record the recipe, topology,
+data, steps, and any unvalidated combinations in the handoff.
+
+## Phase 7: Local review and stack submission
+
+Follow [code_style_checklist.md](references/code_style_checklist.md) for each PR.
+Resolve and read the `pr_review` skill (TorchTitan also names it `pr-review`).
+Use its local branch mode with the PR's actual base and head refs. Review,
+revise, and review again until the current version has local approval, no open
+must-fix findings, and its required checks pass. Re-review affected dependent
+PRs after earlier changes. Submit the stack targeting `upstream/main` only when
+every PR passes; include dependencies, numerical evidence, and review results.
+If a required skill, resource, or decision is missing, report the blocker and
+keep stack submission pending.
+
+## Definition of done
+
+- [ ] A PR stack has working increments and validation criteria for each PR.
+- [ ] Public flavor/build API, model lifecycle, and adapter work for the new model.
+- [ ] Reuse and placement follow current model/config guides; shared callers audited.
+- [ ] Component and full-model forward/backward parity has reproducible inputs,
+      justified tolerances, and appropriate references; MoE routing is validated.
+- [ ] Checkpoint loading and adapter mappings remain compatible for affected models.
+- [ ] Important/new features have meaningful CPU tests, including stateful behavior.
+- [ ] Training hooks, input contracts, and any extra PP state/gradients are validated.
+- [ ] A real-GPU model training test combines FSDP/TP/EP/PP where applicable;
+      its actual config and CI selection are verified.
+- [ ] Offline comparisons cover claimed parallelisms and important combinations,
+      including gradient scaling; the PR records configs, metrics, and evidence.
+- [ ] The chosen debug recipe is demonstrably deterministic across independent
+      remote launches before golden generation; every loss/grad_norm step matches.
+- [ ] A remote debug-recipe golden records loss and grad_norm, provenance, and
+      hardware; a registered regression run passes without export.
+- [ ] Applicable exact-loss/grad_norm or convergence evidence is recorded.
+- [ ] Style and pre-commit checks pass; measured performance uses sufficient steps.
+- [ ] Requested performance comparisons use matched workloads and record results.
+- [ ] Requested scale validation is complete; remaining coverage is stated clearly.
+- [ ] Every PR's current version passes `pr_review` after all required revisions;
+      affected dependent PRs have been re-reviewed before stack submission.
+- [ ] The PR explains the architectural choices and includes numerical evidence.

+# Model Port Cleanup and Review Checklist
+
+Use this checklist for new model code and shared code changed by the port. Follow
+`AGENTS.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and applicable `.claude/rules/` instructions.
+
+## Reuse, placement, and public API
+
+- Reuse existing attention, RoPE, FFN/MoE, embedding, linear, decoder, and adapter
+  helpers. Put shared code in the appropriate base, common, or distributed package.
+  Keep core training and parallelism code PyTorch-native.
+- Put lifecycle contracts in `torchtitan/models/base/`, concrete shared model
+  components in `torchtitan/models/common/`, and distributed helpers in
+  `torchtitan/distributed/`. Keep experiment code in its experiment package.
+- Follow the current package API: `flavors.py` provides `MODEL_FLAVORS` and
+  `build_model_config`; `__init__.py` re-exports these and the model class.
+  Set `state_dict_adapter_cls` on the model class. Add `sharding.py` when shared
+  constructors cannot express the model's sharding.
+- Keep runnable training recipes in `torchtitan_recipes/` and reusable test
+  recipes in `torchtitan_recipes/tests/models/`. Keep integration configs beside
+  their test definitions.
+- Set `param_init` on component configs. Use `_init_self_buffers()` for buffer
+  initialization. Reuse automatic `init_states()` recursion; override it only
+  when ordering requires it. Check weight tying after materialization and loading.
+  Keep routing and conditional computation visible in `forward`.
+
+## Naming, comments, and errors
+
+- Give tensors shape suffixes in new or rewritten model code (`x_BLD`, `q_BLHK`,
+  `out_THV`). Define the letters in each module. They describe logical tensor
+  dimensions and keep their meaning under sharding.
+- Name components for what they compute. Use plain descriptive names for
+  internal components; the package identifies the model. Prefix private helpers
+  with `_` and counts with `num_`, unless matching an upstream API. Follow sibling
+  flavor names.
+- Use `axis`/`axes` for specific DeviceMesh axes and `dim` for tensor dimensions
+  or mesh shape. Match upstream spelling when calling its APIs.
+- Use ASCII in comments and docstrings you add or rewrite. Explain non-obvious
+  math, gradient placements, and workarounds. Remove obvious narration and unused
+  code; keep TODOs for known limitations.
+- Give unfamiliar APIs concise docstrings and a small usage or shape example.
+  Keep function names clear and comments focused on the reason for the behavior.
+- Remove unused settings and casts, fallbacks, or wrappers with no demonstrated
+  need. Preserve supported backends and config paths; audit callers of any
+  intentional removal.
+- Use `ValueError` for bad config or input and `assert` for internal programmer
+  errors. Required config fields must not default to `None`. Put important
+  arguments first and prefer keyword-only options.
+- `dataclasses.replace()` shares nested objects. Copy nested configs when they
+  must change independently.
+
+## Audit changed contracts
+
+- Search all tracked model variants, recipes, and tests when changing a
+  shared component, field, or distributed helper. Update every affected caller.
+- Match sharding input keys to forward parameter names after tensor renames.
+  Validate mesh axes, tensor placements, and gradient placements at DTensor
+  boundaries. Build configs for the recipe's parallelism.
+- Check that compile region names and remat patterns match the intended
+  computation and are applied. Warn when user configuration is skipped.
+- Check optimizer hooks and update/reset timing for stateful features. Check
+  positions, masks, document and modality metadata, and any extra PP state.
+  Trace its gradients and cache cleanup.
+- Test native and HF checkpoint loading, adapter round trips, and tied weights.
+  Check any affected sibling model checkpoints too.
+- Follow [test_coverage.md](test_coverage.md) for CPU feature tests, combined
+  FSDP/TP/EP/PP training on real GPUs where applicable, and a remote debug golden.
+  Verify the actual recipe, model, mesh, feature hooks, and CI suite and hardware.
+- Check component and full-model forward coverage in evaluation and training
+  modes, plus backward coverage for differentiable components and the full
+  training model. Review the offline matrix, reconstructed gradients, global
+  norm ratios, and the reported tolerances and evidence.
+- Before creating a golden, require independent remote debug runs to match
+  exactly for every full-precision loss and grad_norm step. Keep initialization,
+  data order, optimizer, backend, and required features the same.
+- Check that the golden covers all expected loss and grad_norm steps, records
+  run details, and passes an independent replay. Include output and gradient
+  comparisons for new computation and exact loss/grad_norm comparisons for
+  refactors. Add convergence evidence for computation changes.
+
+## Local review and stack submission
+
+Run `pre-commit run --all-files` before review. If local Pyrefly results differ
+from CI, use `/pyrefly_ci_check` when available. Inspect `pyrefly check` output
+and fix environment differences before a hook removes unused ignores. Fix issues
+caused by the port and report any existing or environment failures.
+
+For every PR in the planned stack:
+
+1. Prepare a working increment with its required tests and numerical evidence.
+   Record its base and head refs. The first PR starts from `upstream/main`;
+   later PRs are reviewed against their immediate parent in the stack.
+2. Resolve and read the `pr_review` skill (`pr-review` in TorchTitan's naming).
+   Use local branch mode and explicitly supply the PR's base/head as review
+   context, overriding its single-branch `main...HEAD` default for stacked PRs.
+   Apply current user/repository rules and keep findings local.
+3. Fix each valid must-fix finding in the PR that owns it. Re-run affected tests
+   and numerical comparisons, then amend the appropriate commit(s).
+4. Run `pr_review` again on the revised PR. Repeat review, revise, and re-review
+   until the current version has an **Approve** verdict, no open must-fix items,
+   and all required checks pass. An approval with remaining must-fix edits is
+   still pending; **Request changes** or **Needs discussion** is not a pass.
+5. Update dependent PRs after changes to an earlier PR. Re-review any PR whose
+   code or base changed. Record the reviewed base/head, resolved findings, and
+   final verdict so approval of an old version is not reused.
+6. When every PR passes and the stack is stable, submit it using the repository's
+   supported stack tooling, targeting `upstream/main`. Verify dependencies and
+   that each published PR shows the reviewed changes. Include the scope,
+   numerical evidence, and local review results in each description.
+
+If the review skill, required validation resources, or a necessary decision is
+missing, report the blocker and keep submission pending. Continue independent
+implementation and validation work; never mark an incomplete review as passed.
+
+Record reference and checkpoint revisions, tolerances and measured errors,
+tests run, supported parallelism, and remaining limitations in the PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,212 @@
+# Numerical Parity Against a Reference Model
+
+Compare the same checkpoint and inputs. Find the cause of differences before
+changing the model. Record the reference code and checkpoint revisions,
+model flavor, tokenizer, dtype, attention backend, seed, and input preparation.
+
+## Choose a reference and checkpoint
+
+Choose Hugging Face `transformers`, Megatron-LM/Megatron Core, the model author's
+implementation, SGLang, or vLLM based on support for the variant and features. For
+SGLang/vLLM, record dtype and quantization settings, whether the test uses prefill
+or decode, and the KV-cache state.
+
+Prefer the model's official open weights on Hugging Face Hub when available;
+record the repository ID and pin the checkpoint revision. Use the matching
+model config, tokenizer, and preprocessing assets.
+
+Use references that support training to check gradients, auxiliary objectives,
+and balancing updates. When a training path has no compatible reference, build
+an independent differentiable oracle for the reduced model and its components,
+or record the missing backward check as a required gap.
+
+## Reuse checkpoint converters and comparison scripts
+
+The model package exports `build_model_config`, and its model class defines
+`state_dict_adapter_cls`. The converters in `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/`
+use these APIs. Reuse `convert_from_hf.py` and `convert_to_hf.py`; put changes to
+checkpoint keys and layouts in the adapter and its shared helpers.
+
+For example, after downloading the matching HF assets:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m scripts.checkpoint_conversion.convert_from_hf \
+  assets/hf/Llama-3.1-8B outputs/parity/llama3-8b-dcp \
+  --model_name llama3 --model_flavor 8B
+```
+
+Use the comparison script's supported loading path. Convert to native DCP when
+that path requires it. Start from tracked examples such as
+`numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py` and `numerical_tests_kimi_k3.py`. Check their model
+builders and CLI options before adapting them; older or untracked scripts may
+use a different API.
+
+Keep large checkpoints and activation dumps in generated outputs. Commit small
+test fixtures with reproducible inputs and instructions or a generator to recreate
+them. Reusable comparison scripts belong in `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/`;
+CPU tests belong in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/`. Keep matrix-specific scripts
+and logs in generated outputs and summarize their results in the PR.
+
+## Match inputs, weights, and settings
+
+1. Build the matching config with `ParallelismConfig()`. Match the reference's
+   head layout, context length, norm eps, RoPE settings, routing, auxiliary
+   objectives, and weight tying.
+2. Use the same tokens, images, positions, masks, sequence boundaries, and
+   padding. Check tokenizer and preprocessing separately when necessary.
+3. Materialize and initialize model states before loading the checkpoint. Check
+   that every required weight loads with the right shape and layout, and that
+   the adapter maps the expected keys.
+4. Compare evaluation and training modes separately, with matching dtypes,
+   optimization settings, and relevant random state. Set the seed, normally 42.
+   Use deterministic execution when claiming exact equality; keep
+   `deterministic_warn_only` disabled.
+5. Compare components (RoPE, norms, projections, router), then one block, any
+   vision encoder or projector, and full-model logits. Start with higher
+   precision where supported.
+
+Cover forward outputs for every component and the full model, using existing
+shared tests where they cover unchanged math. For training, compare the normalized
+loss, auxiliary objectives, and state updates through the trainer and optimizer.
+Record the reference and evidence for each component, mode, and full-model check.
+
+## Compare tensors and set tolerances
+
+For intermediate tensors, check shape, finite values, maximum absolute error,
+and relative error. Use `torch.testing.assert_close` with explicit `atol` and
+`rtol`. Justify both for the operation, value magnitude, dtype, and reference.
+Absolute tolerance matters near zero, where relative error is unstable.
+
+For logits, also report probability KL divergence, cosine similarity, and top-k
+agreement. Compute KL from normalized distributions in sufficient precision;
+record its direction and reduction method. Compare the actual logits too:
+adding a constant leaves softmax probabilities unchanged. For example,
+`[1, 2, 3]` and `[101, 102, 103]` have identical probabilities but differ by 100.
+Use tensor errors to validate intermediate activations.
+
+Choose tolerances using a higher-precision reference and an eager baseline in
+the test's dtype where possible. Accumulation order and sequence length affect
+low-precision errors, so calibrate tolerances for each model and operation.
+Record tolerances and measured errors. Investigate failures before changing
+thresholds; do not widen them just to accept the result.
+
+For differentiable components and the full training model, compare parameter
+gradients and input gradients where defined, using the same scalar loss or output
+gradient. Check expected gradient presence, shape, finite values, and tensor errors.
+Match parameter keys and layouts; count tied parameters once. Include custom
+autograd and handwritten kernels. Use `/kernel-numerics-verifier` for a low-precision
+kernel and `/numerics_debugging` to find where unexplained differences start,
+when those skills are available.
+
+## Check MoE routing
+
+Small score differences near a tie can change top-k expert choices. Check score
+math, expert indexing, and selection logic before accepting different choices:
+
+1. Compare scores, biases, selected expert IDs, and mixing weights aligned by
+   expert ID. Include normalization, route scaling, group selection, shared
+   experts, padding, and token filtering where used.
+2. Measure routing agreement per layer and check the score gap between selected
+   and excluded experts. Use higher precision or controlled inputs to check
+   whether score differences explain the changed choices.
+3. In a separate diagnostic run, reuse the reference expert IDs to isolate
+   expert computation and the rest of the network. Report the normal run too,
+   and validate the model's own router independently.
+
+When imposing routing, record whether indices, weights, or both are replaced.
+Overriding weights bypasses router scores and mixing-weight computation; check
+those outputs and gradients separately.
+
+## Offline comparisons across parallelisms
+
+Plan a targeted matrix covering FSDP, TP/SP, EP, PP, and CP where claimed, plus
+important combinations. Start from the validated reference or baseline. Compare
+evaluation outputs and training loss, gradients, and state updates for the same
+logical inputs, checkpoint, effective global batch, and loss normalization.
+Match optimizer/scheduler state and align microbatch accumulation. Record any
+backend or dtype differences.
+
+Capture gradients before clipping and optimizer updates, undoing any configured
+loss scaling as required. Reconstruct shards and apply the declared reductions
+so tensors represent the same logical gradient. Align parameter layouts, count
+tied parameters once, and avoid counting replicated gradients multiple times.
+Compare tensor errors, global gradient norms, per-parameter gradient norm ratios,
+and cosine similarity. Use absolute errors for near-zero gradients. Check selected
+parameter updates under matched optimizer settings as additional evidence.
+
+Large scaling errors, such as a global gradient norm near `2x` the reference,
+require investigation. Apply only the layout conversions and reductions required
+by the parallelism contract; do not rescale gradients to fit the reference.
+For MoE, report normal-routing agreement and use the router checks above to
+diagnose differences.
+
+| Comparison | Acceptance |
+| --- | --- |
+| Different parallelisms or compatible external references | Tensor agreement with justified tolerances and correct gradient scaling |
+| Repeated fixed TorchTitan recipe or non-computation refactor with matching settings/hardware | Bitwise-identical full-precision loss and grad_norm |
+
+Use real communication for distributed numerical evidence. Keep experiment
+scripts, checkpoints, and logs outside the PR. Summarize configurations, GPU
+count/model, compared metrics, tolerances, results, and job/artifact references
+in the PR description. Re-run affected cases after changes and mark missing
+checks as pending rather than passed.
+
+## Check training and distributed execution
+
+Every model port needs a golden from a remote debug run. First prove that
+independent runs have exactly matching full-precision loss and grad_norm at every
+step. Then create the golden. Follow [test_coverage.md](test_coverage.md) for the
+repeatability check, export, replay, files for each GPU architecture, and CI
+registration.
+Reference parity checks correctness; repeated training checks determinism;
+the golden detects later changes to the validated behavior.
+
+After component and forward comparisons pass, validate training. Computation
+changes require loss convergence on representative data. For refactors or
+parallelism changes that preserve computation, compare matching configs with
+seed 42 and deterministic execution. Require bitwise-identical loss and grad_norm
+when parallelisms and GPU settings match. Use full-precision TensorBoard values.
+
+For an existing model, adapt this command to the before and after refs
+and a recipe present in both checkouts:
+
+```bash
+python3 scripts/loss_compare.py upstream/main HEAD \
+  --baseline-module=torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.llama3 \
+  --baseline-config=llama3_debugmodel --steps=10 \
+  --metrics=loss,grad_norm --assert-equal
+```
+
+Set `--baseline-ngpus` and `--test-ngpus` to each run's GPU count. The script
+enables deterministic execution and defaults to comparing loss; request both
+metrics. For recipes with transforms, check whether seed creation needs a
+matching `--seed-module` and `--seed-config`. See `scripts/loss_compare.py` and
+the integration suite's `loss_compare_seed_config` examples.
+
+## Checkpoint and layout checks
+
+- **Native DCP compatibility.** If native checkpoint names, shapes, or parameter
+  layouts change, test loading and regenerate affected converted fixtures.
+  Check the actual keys after changing the module tree. Unexplained missing or
+  unexpected keys, or uninitialized weights, fail the comparison. Preserve
+  loading of previously supported checkpoints.
+- **Complex RoPE buffers.** Casting to a real dtype can discard the imaginary
+  part of a complex cache. Set buffer dtypes through the model lifecycle and
+  rebuild buffers before loading weights. Preserve their intended dtype and
+  keep loaded parameters unchanged while fixing a buffer.
+- **Tied embeddings.** Match `Decoder.Config.enable_weight_tying` to the
+  reference's `tie_word_embeddings`. Check that weights stay shared through
+  construction, materialization, initialization, and loading. Equal values in
+  separate parameters do not share gradients. Reuse adapter support for omitted
+  tied output weights.
+- **Norm variants.** Match eps and the weight convention. Account for offsets
+  such as `(1 + weight) * norm(x)` in the math or adapter.
+- **RoPE and projections.** Check partial rotation, adjacent-pair or split-half
+  rotation, multimodal position axes, GQA head order, fused QKV splits, and gated
+  projections. Reuse fused-linear adapter helpers.
+- **Packed and distributed inputs.** Match document boundaries, position resets,
+  masks and offsets, padding, CP input and label sharding, and recurrence resets.
+  Test the selected backend's metadata handling.
+- **Config and sharding.** Build configs for the intended parallelism. Rebuild
+  them when sequence or expert parallelism changes. Preserve component sharding
+  when applying transforms.

+# Model Port Test Coverage
+
+Add three types of tests for every model port. Record what each test covers, its
+recipe, expected result, hardware, and whether it has run. Keep the model's
+important features in the smaller debug model, including any MoE routing,
+balancing, hybrid attention, auxiliary objectives, or multimodal inputs.
+
+Also run reference parity and the offline parallelism matrix during enablement.
+Commit the focused feature tests, combined integration test, and numerical
+golden. Keep scripts and logs for the wider matrix in generated outputs and
+include its evidence in the PR description.
+
+## 1. Important feature tests, mostly CPU
+
+List new math, routing, state updates, and checkpoint behavior. Reuse tests
+that exercise those paths and add focused tests where coverage is missing. Put
+tests for shared components in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/` and tests
+for individual models in their CPU test packages; extend shared config/adapter
+tests as needed.
+
+Use small inputs and expected results calculated by hand or by an independent
+reference algorithm. Choose cases that expose likely errors, and check gradients
+for new operations that require them. Include edge cases.
+
+Test stateful features through the trainer and optimizer. Check when statistics
+accumulate, when updates and resets happen, evaluation behavior, checkpoint
+loading, and resetting temporary state. Recomputing activations must not count
+statistics twice.
+
+Examples:
+
+- Quantile balancing: quantile math and state updates.
+- New attention math: output and gradient checks against a simple reference.
+
+Keep feature tests runnable on CPU. Also check outputs and gradients of custom
+CUDA kernels on GPU. Check that state shared across ranks stays consistent in
+the combined training test.
+
+Run the relevant CPU tests and confirm CI runs them. The CPU workflow uses
+`pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu`.
+
+## 2. Combined parallelism training on real GPUs
+
+Add one training test that enables FSDP, TP, EP, and PP together for
+an MoE model, normally on a remote node with 8 H100s. For a dense model, cover
+FSDP/TP/PP and record EP as not applicable. Use this run to catch interactions
+between parallelisms. Add separate tests for features it cannot cover.
+
+Build the parallelism config first and pass it to the model's flavor builder.
+This is a valid starting configuration for 8 GPUs:
+
+```python
+from torchtitan.config.parallelism import ParallelismConfig
+
+parallelism = ParallelismConfig(
+    data_parallel_replicate_degree=1,
+    data_parallel_shard_degree=2,
+    tensor_parallel_degree=2,
+    expert_parallel_degree=2,
+    pipeline_parallel_degree=2,
+    context_parallel_degree=1,
+    pipeline_parallel_schedule="1F1B",
+    num_pp_microbatches=4,
+)
+```
+
+The GPU count is `dp_replicate * dp_shard * cp * tp * pp = 8`.
+EP shares the ranks used by `dp_shard`, `cp`, and `tp`:
+`edp_shard * ep = dp_shard * cp * tp`. Here expert FSDP has `edp_shard = 2`.
+Setting EP=4 gives `edp_shard = 1`. Choose degrees that fit the expert count,
+attention heads, and model dimensions, then check the resulting sharding.
+See Qwen3.5 in `tests/integration_tests/models.py` for an example with
+FSDP=2, TP=2, EP=4, PP=2.
+
+Use a supported pipeline schedule, enough layers for every stage, and enough
+tokens for the microbatches. Train for at least 10 optimizer steps with the new
+features enabled. Check finite loss and grad_norm, successful backward and
+optimizer steps, and feature updates across steps. Check expected behavior,
+such as matching router state across ranks.
+
+Register an importable recipe factory in an `IntegrationTestDefinition` in
+`tests/integration_tests/models.py` or `tests/integration_tests/h100.py`.
+Set `ngpu=8` and `use_real_pg=True`. Check the actual model, parallelism, sharding,
+features, and optimizer. Confirm the test runs with real communication on the
+intended GPUs. PP and checkpoint tests need `use_real_pg=True`.
+
+Choose PP splits that test state passed between layers. Kimi K3's attention
+residual cache needs multiple virtual stages, exact gradient routing, and cleanup
+between microbatches, between steps, and after evaluation. Check input preparation
+too: Qwen3.5 uses different positions for attention masks and MRoPE, and keeps
+vision gradients connected when images or videos are absent. Packed compression
+and recurrence must match processing each document separately, including short
+documents and incomplete groups. Add CP or modality tests when the combined
+recipe cannot cover them.
+
+Record which optimizers are tested. Kimi K3's combined TP test uses AdamW, and
+a separate test covers DistMuon. Add another recipe if the combined test cannot
+cover a required feature or optimizer.
+
+The H100 workflow calls `.github/scripts/run_8xgpu_integration_tests.sh`, which
+runs the `h100` suite. Register the test in that suite and check the filters,
+GPU count, and disabled settings so CI runs it.
+
+### Offline numerical comparisons
+
+Follow [numerical_parity.md](numerical_parity.md) for component and full-model
+forward/backward checks across each claimed parallelism and important
+combinations. Compare matching logical inputs, global batches, checkpoints,
+and loss normalization. Check reconstructed gradients and global norm ratios
+with justified tolerances; different parallelisms need numerical agreement.
+Exact repeatability remains required for the fixed debug recipe below.
+
+Add comparisons as later PRs add parallelisms or kernels. Record recipes, mesh
+settings, metrics, tolerances, results, and job/artifact references in the PR.
+Keep matrix-specific test scripts and logs outside the PR.
+
+## 3. Numerical golden baseline from a remote debug run
+
+### Prove the debug recipe is deterministic
+
+After reference parity and feature tests pass, choose a small debug recipe that
+keeps the important computation and state updates. Enable deterministic execution
+and prove that independent runs produce identical metrics before creating a golden.
+
+Pin the recipe. Record the source commit, GPU model and count, parallelism,
+PyTorch, CUDA and dependency versions, dtype, attention backend, compile/remat
+settings, optimizer and scheduler, tokenizer and data revisions, input order,
+and initialization. Set `config.debug.seed = 42` and
+`config.debug.deterministic = True`; never enable `deterministic_warn_only`.
+Use the same hardware, settings, and data order for replay.
+
+Run at least two independent training jobs on the target remote GPUs, with the
+same code and config and at least 10 optimizer steps each. Start with fresh
+optimizer, scheduler, router/balancer, and dataloader state. Use reproducible
+initialization or the same pinned checkpoint. Give each run its own output
+directory. When using generated seed checkpoints, independently recreate the
+checkpoint for each run to check initialization too.
+
+Save temporary loss and grad_norm traces in the run outputs. Both runs must have
+the same expected step numbers, finite values, and bitwise-identical loss and
+grad_norm at every step. Compare full-precision TensorBoard values; stdout rounds
+them. Record the runs and comparison result. Repeat if differences are intermittent.
+
+`loss_compare.py` needs import/export for a same-config `. .` comparison. First
+capture one run's metrics, then compare a new run against them. Define importable
+debug and matching seed recipe factories before using this template. Adjust the
+module, hardware, and GPU count:
+
+```bash
+python3 scripts/loss_compare.py . . \
+  --baseline-module=tests.integration_tests.h100 \
+  --baseline-config=new_model_debugmodel_all_parallelism \
+  --seed-config=new_model_debugmodel_seed \
+  --baseline-ngpus=8 --test-ngpus=8 --steps=10 --metrics=loss,grad_norm \
+  --job-dump-folder=outputs/new-model-repeatability/run-a \
+  --output-folder=outputs/new-model-repeatability/run-a-logs \
+  --export-result=outputs/new-model-repeatability/run-a-metrics.txt
+
+python3 scripts/loss_compare.py . . \
+  --baseline-module=tests.integration_tests.h100 \
+  --baseline-config=new_model_debugmodel_all_parallelism \
+  --seed-config=new_model_debugmodel_seed \
+  --baseline-ngpus=8 --test-ngpus=8 --steps=10 --metrics=loss,grad_norm \
+  --job-dump-folder=outputs/new-model-repeatability/run-b \
+  --output-folder=outputs/new-model-repeatability/run-b-logs \
+  --import-result=outputs/new-model-repeatability/run-a-metrics.txt \
+  --assert-equal
+```
+
+These commands independently create seed checkpoints and capture temporary
+metrics from the same recipe. Keep the required features, optimizer, and backend
+active. If the runs differ, investigate data order, initialization, state updates,
+kernel reductions/atomics, routing ties, and compile/remat behavior. Use
+`/numerics_debugging` when available. Fix the cause and repeat the check. Keep
+exact equality checks, required state updates, and the model's own routing;
+never enable `deterministic_warn_only`.
+
+Use the combined training recipe for the golden when it passes this check. If
+its parallelism or backend cannot be made repeatable, record the limitation and
+use a separate numerical recipe that keeps the important features. Prove that
+recipe repeats exactly before creating its golden.
+
+### Create the golden after the runs match
+
+Use the integration runner and `scripts/loss_compare.py` to export full-precision
+TensorBoard loss and grad_norm to a small text file. The runner adds the config,
+GPU count, and parallelism header. Record other run details in comments or
+documentation beside the golden. Keep large logs, checkpoints, and TensorBoard
+files in persistent remote storage.
+
+Define both recipe factories before using this registration template:
+
+```python
+from tests.integration_tests import IntegrationTestDefinition
+
+IntegrationTestDefinition(
+    configs=[new_model_debugmodel_all_parallelism],
+    test_name="new_model_fsdp+tp+ep+pp",
+    test_descr="New model combined parallelism and numerical regression",
+    ngpu=8,
+    use_real_pg=True,
+    golden_numerics_path=(
+        "tests/assets/losses/real_pg/{gpu_arch}/new_model_all_parallelism.txt"
+    ),
+    loss_compare_seed_config=new_model_debugmodel_seed,
+)
+```
+
+A test with a golden must have exactly one config. The `real_pg` runner creates
+a single-GPU seed checkpoint by default. The seed recipe must build the same
+model and weights with parallelism disabled and no transforms that need multiple
+GPUs. Preserve feature math and initialization. Set `loss_compare_seed_config`
+when the training recipe cannot create this seed. Keep stateful features active.
+
+After the repeatability check passes and the test is registered in the `h100`
+suite, export on the remote GPU node using its supported launcher and the
+validated recipe. Replace the template names and paths. Use an empty output
+directory for each run:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m tests.integration_tests.run_tests outputs/new-model-export \
+  --test_suite h100 --test_name new_model_fsdp+tp+ep+pp \
+  --execution_mode real_pg --gpu_arch_type cuda --gpu_arch h100 \
+  --ngpu 8 --no-parallel --export-numerics
+```
+
+Set the recipe's `training.steps` to at least 10 before export. The runner writes
+the result to `outputs/new-model-export/real_pg/h100/` using the golden's filename.
+Check every expected step, both metrics, run settings, and enabled features. Copy
+the checked file into the registered `tests/assets/losses/real_pg/h100/` path.
+Keep separate goldens for each GPU architecture and communication mode.
+
+Replay against the committed golden using another empty output directory:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m tests.integration_tests.run_tests outputs/new-model-replay \
+  --test_suite h100 --test_name new_model_fsdp+tp+ep+pp \
+  --execution_mode real_pg --gpu_arch_type cuda --gpu_arch h100 \
+  --ngpu 8 --no-parallel
+```
+
+Set `golden_numerics_path` and confirm the replay log shows that the golden was
+imported and compared. Require matching step numbers and exact full-precision
+loss and grad_norm at every step. Check the `# step loss grad_norm` header so
+both metrics are covered. CI must compare against the golden without export.
+
+Investigate differences before updating the golden. For an intentional computation
+or dependency change, include new numerical checks, convergence evidence where
+required, old and new values at each step, and the reason for the update. Keep
+the old golden while debugging.
+
+## Coverage and completion evidence
+
+Maintain a compact table for every component and the full model. Separate
+evaluation and training checks, including forward outputs, gradients where
+defined, and state updates. Link shared tests when they cover unchanged math.
+Mark a check passed only after validating the intended recipe and feature path.
+
+| PR / component or model | Mode | Forward / backward / state check | Reference and revision | Recipe / parallelism | Evidence / status |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Fill per checked case | Evaluation or training | Compared tensors or state | Framework or independent oracle | Factory and mesh | Result, artifact, or pending reason |
+
+- Tests for each feature, including new math, gradients, and state updates.
+- Combined training recipe, actual mesh, hardware, steps, and CI selection.
+- Offline parallelism comparisons, with gradient scaling checks and measured
+  errors against justified tolerances.
+- Independent remote debug runs, with exact loss and grad_norm comparisons at
+  every expected step before golden generation.
+- Golden file, run details, and a successful independent replay that compares
+  full-precision loss and grad_norm.
+- Checks not yet run and unsupported combinations.
+- Local review results for each PR's current base/head, with all must-fix
+  findings resolved before submitting the stack.
+
+If remote GPUs are unavailable, prepare the tests and recipes and list the
+pending GPU runs. Mark golden validation complete only after an independent
+replay passes.
